summary: Keep the unstopped mechanical gate runners in a trigger-kept table so the reconciler's list stops parsing every gate request in history

replay.detail: No claim replay changes. The explicit projection rebuild refills the table from the claims and marks the copy complete.

schema.detail: New local tables local_gate_runners (one row per exec, loop-metric or model gate request with no stop observed on its subject, with a subject index) and local_gate_runners_backfill (the ceiling and cursor of a one-time copy), and three triggers on claims (insert, delete, and update of id, subject, kind, origin or body) that keep the first. No schema-version change. The triggers and the ceiling, the newest claim they did not see, commit together in the store open; the gate requests at or below the ceiling are copied after the API serves, 256 per background writer loan with a 50 ms pause, each re-checked for a stop under the writer. Until the copy completes the reconciler lists gate runners from the claims, as before.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest changes; the table is local and never replicated or digested. Mixed-version safe: the triggers live in the database, so an older binary that writes claims keeps the table exact, and a newer one reads it.

compatibility.detail: No client, protocol or pairing changes. The reconciler sees the same gate runners as before.

downtime.detail: No added startup work: the one-time copy runs after the API serves. Once it completes (the first minutes of the first start of this build), the reconciler's first pass after every start, and its full pass every 5 minutes, list gate runners from the table instead of a query that took 9.2 s on a busy member's store in the minute after a restart.

manual.detail: No operator actions or configuration changes; identity and stored state are preserved.

recovery.detail: Swapping back is supported: an older build reads the claims as before, and the triggers it keeps firing cost one indexed probe per gate request or runtime observation written.
